foia_totals.summary: FOIA as of 2026-06-30, 6 files: 7(a) 1,961,455 rows, 1,718,665 loans net of cancellations, volume $527,243,968,642, 220,688 CHGOFF rows; 504 229,049 rows, 196,735 loans, volume $129,055,577,411, 12,169 CHGOFF rows; approval FY 1991 to 2026.

notes: Method: sample values are re-derived by a direct per-row scan of the raw CSVs; a second route (full state/county/NAICS/FY cube) re-derives every value of all 16 series; the two routes agree on 352 of 352 sampled cells. Neither route uses scripts/markets*.py or any data/markets file other than sources.json, geographies.json, naics-map.json and the register series being checked.

Sample design: seed 20261016, python random.Random(seed).random() only; 16 series x [2 us, 4 state, 3 single-county, 4 multi-county county-set, 4 cbsa-delineation market (92 of the 116 are multi-county), 2 cross-state or part, 3 CT component]; class drawn 20% 'all', 35% exact, 25% partial, 20% proxy; window drawn from the 3 windows (once each) and, in the four count series that have it, by_fy (3 slots) for additive series, pooled FY2011-2020 for rates; 75% of draws required a non-zero register value (so matches are not just zero equals zero), 25% unconstrained. Sampled non-zero register cells: 292 of 352.

Layout read from the register and geographies.json: windows ['all', 'fy2016_2025', 'fy2021_2025'] (read from every series' own 'windows' key and checked against its prose); by_fy arrays only in ['loans', 'cancelled', 'disbursed', 'chgoff_n']; 225 summed markets from markets[].foia.strings ({'cbsa': 116, 'county': 43, 'county-set': 62, 'cross-state': 4}); 16 Connecticut components from foia.ct.legacy / foia.ct.pr; 4 cross-state state parts (kind cross-state only, strings spanning two or more states); 158 multi-county markets by distinct (state, county) strings; 14 cbsa markets span two or more states.
